title: Repair one communicating-artery connection from MRA evidence
hypothesis: Given one small MRA region and a proposed vessel mask, an agent can use image evidence to repair a broken or false connection while preserving an annotated asymmetric or incomplete Circle of Willis configuration.
why_hard: Not established. The synthetic gap passes with Terra/high and an ordinary image-guided baseline. The unchanged-case Terra output fails preservation, but follows visible signal omitted from the reference near L-ACA; clinical/anatomical adjudication is unresolved. Published TopCoW errors do not transfer automatically to this binary-mask task.
next_action: Bounded feasibility experiment complete; no trial queued. Retain V01 as calibration and hold V02 as a reference disagreement. Any future promotion requires independent review of the added L-ACA-adjacent structure and a separately admitted natural segmentation-model error with reproducible prediction provenance.

notes: BR-025 curated four technically checked TopCoW MRA references (004, 007, 009, 012); 30 selected files, 211.86 MB, CRC/SHA-256 checked. BR-026 froze a 200-voxel synthetic right-Pcom gap in 007 and unchanged left-only Pcom case 012. Twenty author control observations and four matched Docker oracle/nop controls pass expectations. Two fresh Terra/high runs complete normally on identical frozen bytes: V01 passes in 300.813 s, restores 198/200 voxels, 100% centerline coverage, no collateral edits. V02 fails in 646.152 s after 244 additions (12.903 mm3), but preserves the absent right Pcom and existing branch routes. Added structure contacts only source L-ACA, follows visible signal and lacks independent expert adjudication; retain score failure without claiming a confirmed anatomical reasoning error. Public-input image baseline passes both. Artifact replays match and runtime model/effort metadata agree; no source-answer retrieval observed. No natural prediction error, true false-bridge repair, independent clinical validation or general capability estimate. No retry, Sol escalation, publication or submission promotion.
